quiz_items.question: Which potency level does the zygote have?
quiz_items.reviewed_explanation: The zygote is totipotent: it can differentiate into any cell type, including cells of the placenta.

quiz_items.question: What can pluripotent stem cells NOT form?

options.text: Any cell type of the body

quiz_items.reviewed_explanation: Pluripotent stem cells can become any cell type in the body but cannot form the trophoblast and extra-embryonic cells such as the placenta.

quiz_items.question: Which example is given for unipotent cells?
quiz_items.reviewed_explanation: Unipotent is the lowest level: the cell differentiates into only a single cell type, for example cardiomyocytes.

quiz_items.question: Which set of genes is used to reprogram adult cells into iPS cells?
quiz_items.reviewed_explanation: iPS cells are created by reprogramming adult cells with the pluripotent genes Oct4, Sox2, C-Myc and Klf4.

quiz_items.question: From which structure are embryonic stem cells harvested?
quiz_items.reviewed_explanation: Embryonic stem cells are harvested from the blastocyst, a 3-5 day embryo.

tutor_items.question: What are the three main properties of stem cells?
tutor_items.reviewed_explanation: The notes list three properties: self-renewal (a stem cell generates a specialized daughter cell and a new copy of itself), differentiation (it becomes a specialized cell) and potency (its ability to differentiate into specialized cell types).

tutor_items.question: What is stem cell mobilization in hematopoietic stem cell therapy?
tutor_items.expected_answer: Using medications such as G-CSF and chemotherapy to move HSCs from the bone marrow into the bloodstream.
tutor_items.reviewed_explanation: Mobilization is the process of using medications such as growth factor (G-CSF) and chemotherapy to move hematopoietic stem cells from the bone marrow into the bloodstream, before collection.

tutor_items.question: How does an oligopotent stem cell differ from a multipotent one? Give the example from the notes.
tutor_items.expected_answer: It is similar but more limited; example: lymphoid stem cell giving T and B cells.
tutor_items.reviewed_explanation: Oligopotent stem cells are similar to multipotent cells but more limited. The example given is the lymphoid stem cell, which gives rise to T and B cells.
